content: The meeting and its associated report, along with relevant publications or work products, included considerations for managing conflicts of interest. Partial Exclusion: In cases of limited involvement, experts were excluded from portions of the meeting or work where a conflict of interest was identified. Additionally, they were not allowed to participate in the decision-making process. Any reported conflicts of interest were disclosed publicly to other meeting participants and documented in the meeting report and related publications or work products. The partial exclusion process was carefully monitored during the meeting. Total Exclusion: In cases of significant conflict, the expert was excluded from the meeting entirely. Potential Conflicts of Interest (External Review Group Members) 1. Paulo Abrao Ferreira: No conflicts of interest reported. 2. Amit Goel: No conflicts of interest reported. 3. Muhammad Radzi Abu Hassan: No conflicts of interest reported. 4. N. Kumarasamy: No conflicts of interest reported. 5. Brian J. McMahon: No conflicts of interest reported. 6. Ponsiano Ocama: No conflicts of interest reported. 7. Cesar Cabezas Sanchez: No conflicts of interest reported. 8. Gamal Shiha: No conflicts of interest reported. 9. Mark Sonderup: Reported a conflict of interest related to research support. Specifically, a grant of $7,500 was provided by the Gilead Foundation to initiate the ECHO SSA project, which ended in 2019. Additionally, a travel grant of $1,500 for transportation and accommodation to attend a conference was provided by the Gilead Foundation in 2022. 10. David Thomas: Reported a financial, non-significant conflict of interest. Abbott Diagnostics donated HBV testing for 12,000 specimens in Nigeria as part of a research collaboration. No monetary exchange occurred, and the exact value of the testing support is unknown. 11. Pham Thi Thanh Thuy: Reported a significant financial conflict of interest. A research grant of $2 million over four years (2022–2026) was provided by Gilead Sciences to support a research unit and staff for implementing a new model of care for managing viral hepatitis in Vietnam and the Philippines. 12. Thomas Tu: Reported a significant financial conflict of interest. Employment at the Westmead Institute for Medical Research provided an annual salary of 113,334 Australian dollars. Consultation fees included $4,000 from Excision Biosciences (ongoing), 2,100 Australian dollars from Gilead in 2020, and 3,502 Australian dollars from GSK in 2023. Research support included a five-year grant for testing an antiviral therapy developed by Excision Biosciences against hepatitis B in cell culture models. Additionally, a one-year grant of 50,000 Australian dollars (2022–2023) was provided by the Gastroenterological Society of Australia for a project titled Curing Chronic Hepatitis B by Targeting Virus Reservoirs. 13. Michael Vinikoor: Reported a financial, non-significant conflict of interest. Non-monetary support included $5,000 provided to the research unit in 2021 and $1,000 provided to the External Review Group member in 2022 by Cepheid.
